items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: such personalities as Edgar Guest and Guy Lombardo and Norman Rockwell were essentially the same, that they represented exactly the same point of view and appealed to the same people

ctx.x: Al, I'd like to ask you a question that interests me very much. What kind of a feeling do you get when you listen to, for instance, Big Spiderman solo? What kind of emotional fulfillment does that represent? What kind of people seem to be attracted to that kind of sound?

Well, I think that I understand the question. And, of course, as you understand, it's not my kind of people. That is, that I don't really respond emotionally to the Bix sound, although I understand it, I think. And I find it very interesting, but purely on an intellectual basis. But I don't have any visceral reaction to Bix. items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: I would consider it to be the suggestion that Guy Lombardo is the leader of a jazz band to have very tenuous merit.

ctx.x: Might they be using it as a general descriptive term?

Well, I would hope that they would do that, except for the fact that as it is used, it is in fact not descriptive of anything. For instance, I would consider it to be the suggestion that Guy Lombardo is the leader of a jazz band to have very tenuous merit. Yeah, I think... Except for the fact that it, in fact, is and has been used by those people who consider anything other than concert music to be jazz, which represents a substantial group in our population.
